title: Сто двадцать граммов до победы  (One Hundred Twenty Grams from Victory)

segments.t: After Vika tells the waiter to bring the bill to Lavrov, Barinov gloats to Mikhail that the prefect gave up with a hundred and twenty grams of steak left. When they go to the restroom to check on him, the prefect does not answer.
Тут ещё сто двадцать граммов осталось.
Николай Марьянович, с вами всё хорошо?
Ему стало плохо от твоего спора.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Girls, order, do not be shy.' The meaning hinges on 'girls' working together with 'be shy' in spoken Russian.
'Give the bill to Lavrov.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'score' and 'to give' in a few short words.
'Well then, did you lose?' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'lost' in spoken Russian.
'He will come right back and finish eating.' Here Mikhail anchors the thought on 'now' and finishes on 'will finish eating', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Тут ещё сто двадцать граммов осталось.
'There are still a hundred and twenty grams left here.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'here' and 'else' in a few short words.
'Nikolai Maryanovich, are you in here?' Mikhail chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'here' to keep a polite distance.
Николай Марьянович, с вами всё хорошо?
'Nikolai Maryanovich, is everything alright with you?' The meaning hinges on 'Nikolai' working together with 'well' in spoken Russian. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Why is he not answering?' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'is responsible' to negate the statement.
'Open the door, please!' The grammar packs 'open' and 'please' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ему стало плохо от твоего спора.
'He got sick from your bet.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'to him' and 'to become' in a few short words. Mikhail answers right away.
'Break the lock faster!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'faster' before landing on 'lock'.
'Call an ambulance!' The meaning hinges on 'to cause' working together with 'help' in spoken Russian. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Тут ещё сто двадцать граммов осталось.
Николай Марьянович, с вами всё хорошо?
Ему стало плохо от твоего спора.
Pulling the unconscious prefect out of the restroom stall, Barinov and Mikhail call paramedics to the restaurant immediately. Until next time!
